decision: Validate live preflight identity before using title/profile or starting chat: YouTube exact requested video; SOOP live ID and uploader must agree with the canonical requested channel and station broadcast, and with a scheduled expected broadcast if present. Invalid/missing/mismatched identity is an explicit failure, not an empty result or a guessed ID.

Supply exactly one --break-match-filters argument to the actual receiver, ANDing is_live and strict anchored id; SOOP also requires exact validated uploader_id. Construct only from strictly validated bounded IDs, use regex anchors to avoid numeric coercion, and do not include missing-field allowance, user filter fragments, cookies, exec/postprocessing hooks, a second receiver or receipt files.

The existing direct receiver-to-FFmpeg pipe is unchanged. A receiver rejected by this guard produces no media and yields a short explicit changed/unconfirmed-broadcast error without exposing stderr titles/URLs. Cancellation and process-tree drain remain unchanged.

Add optional/default broadcastId to the independently owned platform MediaJob/LibraryItem and frontend DTO. VOD and older items without proof remain None. New scheduled jobs stay None while resolving; after a committed segment from the guarded receiver exists, persist the confirmed ID before copying its first recording segment. Manual recording begun after playing may copy the already confirmed identity. On persistence failure preserve inputs and fail; do not claim recording success.

Completion copies broadcastId from the current durable job, not a stale Recorder.job snapshot. Retry/restart preserves the recorded ID, never queries today's broadcast or backfills old recordings. Invalid optional identity is discarded without losing an otherwise usable legacy media record.

No grouping UI/API is added in this batch. Subsequent group summary/member pagination must use provider/live/broadcast and SOOP channel identity, never title/date/channel alone or just100loaded files.
